analysis:
Both supplied units are head-side excerpts of docs/reference/configuration.md. The file changes are documentation only: the 'Last updated' date, and the 'Cluster runtime facts' section (head ~923-1015), which is outside the excerpted line ranges. That section now says a signed release can register cluster_runtime via POST /v1/releases, and that the coordinator derives cluster approvals, pair-serving grants and parity qualifications from it. No code, key handling, endpoint or authorization logic changes in the supplied evidence.

The visible excerpt (lines 1-484) repeats existing documented config: GLM local qualification, prefix-cache default-on with DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 (consistent with T-041), add-on hold socket (TB-012/T-059), sandbox CLI (TB-013/T-061), endpoint resumption and logout (A-008, T-053), and App Attest worker opt-ins (TB-011). I found nothing that contradicts the threat model, such as new env passthrough, loosened bounds or weakened trust claims.

Remaining question for integration: the changed cluster-runtime block is not visible in these units. It describes a new trust path, where a release payload (A-005 release API key, A-011/A-017 registries) auto-derives cluster approvals and pair-serving grants. That path is backend-owned and out of scope for this provider-focused model, and the actual implementation is not supplied. Any threat-model update for it, or for who authorizes cluster_runtime in release registration, should be checked against the full patch and platform-side code. No finding is raised, since there is no evidence of a regression in the visible text.
